name: dev.telara/gitlab-mr-review-queue
description: Fetch open merge requests for a GitLab project, join each to its source branch's latest CI pipeline status, and rank them into a review queue using a deterministic urgency score (failing pipeline, staleness since last activity, and — for the single longest-untouched merge request each run — whether any reviewer has commented). Read-only; never merges, approves, comments, or triggers pipelines. Fully deterministic: no model reasoning is used.

transform.program:
# rank.star — deterministic capping + stalest-candidate selection.
# TAP transform contract: step params arrive as predeclared globals (merge_requests,
# max_mrs); the value assigned to `result` is the step's output. No I/O, no imports —
# Starlark is sandboxed by construction; the runtime enforces step/time ceilings.
#
# `stalest` is ALWAYS a resolvable dict, even when there are no open merge requests
# (a sentinel with iid 0) — this keeps the downstream `notes` api: step's params free
# of a null dereference regardless of whether the engine actually honors `when:` on an
# api: step (see workflow.yaml's `notes` step comment / README SPEC-FEEDBACK #4).
_SENTINEL = {"iid": 0, "author": "", "updated_at": ""}

def _stalest(mrs):
    stalest = _SENTINEL
    for m in mrs:
        if stalest["iid"] == 0 or m["updated_at"] < stalest["updated_at"]:
            stalest = m
    return stalest

def _rank(mrs, max_mrs):
    capped = mrs[:max_mrs]
    return {
        "capped": capped,
        "stalest": _stalest(capped),
        "has_mrs": len(capped) > 0,
        "total_open": len(mrs),
    }

result = _rank(merge_requests, max_mrs)

inputs.name: max_mrs
inputs.description: Cap on open merge requests considered per run, applied after fetching

inputs.name: project_id
inputs.description: GitLab project ID (numeric) or URL-encoded path like 'group%2Fproject'

inputs.name: stale_before
inputs.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; merge requests with no activity since this time are flagged stale
